significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that the independently annotated "specification gap" predicts reasoning failure and that "precisifying the language ... recovers most lost accuracy," a form-(iii) predictive relation supplemented by a causal input intervention rather than merely an ambiguity-existence claim. It would establish a behavioral phenomenon and an input-side causal explanation—not an internal model mechanism—and the alternative-reading match would constrain how benchmark errors are attributed by separating pragmatic mis-resolution from failed computation; this matters alongside AmbigQA (Min et al., 2020), which treats ambiguous questions as admitting multiple valid answers. The claim is determinate enough for true and false states to differ, while a negative result would usefully show that explicit interpretation control does not explain much of the error and thus favor genuine reasoning failure, although "large fraction" and "most" lack quantitative thresholds. Topic substitution lowers the assessment from what the broad language–intelligence topic might suggest: removing the specification-gap law and intended-versus-alternative decomposition leaves only a generic ambiguity hypothesis at the topic median, whereas these specific additions justify a score above it.

reach.justification: The main reusable handle is the per-problem "SpecificationGap = number (and weighted type) of latent choice points," accompanied by the "interpretation-error rate" and the design action of precisifying an intended reading. SpecificationGap is ex ante because it can screen or flag a problem before solving, while the error-rate decomposition is post hoc; the former gives benchmark designers, auditors, and prompt-system builders an action window to rewrite or gate underspecified items. After re-extraction, the asserted directional relation—more latent choices predict more failures and explicit precisification restores accuracy—would predict what to expect across the claimed arithmetic, temporal, and reference/logic families, though its weights and effect sizes may require recalibration and the claim expressly notes that open-ended naturalistic text may not support exhaustive enumeration. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic relationship between language and intelligence supplies no handle, while this claim's ex-ante metric and cross-task design rule support moderate-to-strong reach rather than topic-derived credit.
